mechanism: Bind the lower three grey cells to a halfturned L covering C and E; confuse a halfturn with the requested vertical reflection.
primary_mathematical_proof: Zero-based grey cells: (1,3),(2,3),(2,2),(0,1),(1,1),(0,0). True reflection x=3 gives (4,3),(3,3),(3,2),(5,1),(4,1),(5,0). Letters A=(3,3),B=(4,3),C=(5,0),D=(4,1),E=(4,0); E alone uncovered. False lower-L halfturn gives(5,1),(5,0),(4,0), with upper L correctly reflected, so A/B/C/E covered and D omitted. Six existing edge intervals change no grey fill, grid, crease or letter.
marker_roles: Red source lower-L bottom cell(0,0) BOTTOM edge is the first halfturn source member.
Red target cell(5,1) TOP edge is its false halfturn destination, using (c,r)->(5-c,1-r).
Blue source cell(0,1) BOTTOM edge identifies the common corner member of the lower L.
Blue target C cell(5,0) TOP edge is its halfturn destination, reversing vertical order as well as horizontal order.
Green source cell(1,1) BOTTOM edge identifies the upper-right arm member.
Green target E cell(4,0) TOP edge maps that arm below C rather than to the true D row; thus the false lower L covers C/E and misses D.
